title: Progress toward compiling Linux with gccrs

The gccrs project, which is creating a Rust frontend for the GCC compiler, has spent the first half of 2026 focusing on compiling the Linux kernel. By testing the compiler against the kernel crates, the development team has made significant progress toward generating correct code for other Rust programs. As detailed in the project's weekly and monthly reports, this effort has uncovered and resolved problems in areas such as attribute handling (described in the report for February), name resolution, and resource management (both detailed in the May report). Currently, the compiler can only handle simple standalone programs, but that situation could change rapidly in the coming months.

The drive to compile the Rust components of the Linux kernel stems from the new toolchain requirements brought by Rust's introduction into the kernel. Currently, developers must use the LLVM-based rustc compiler (although rustc does have experimental, in-progress support for using GCC as a backend via rust_codegen_gcc). While LLVM is supported by the kernel, a GCC-based alternative is necessary to support architectures not targeted by LLVM and to integrate with GCC's existing plugin ecosystem. As the kernel's Rust integration matures, toolchain flexibility and the availability of a GCC-based compiler have become priorities for Linux distributions.

Reorganizing milestones

Compiler frontend projects often track their progress against the release cycle of their target backend. In its March 2026 report, the gccrs team announced a change in project management, opting to organize its work into three capability-based milestones rather than targeting specific GCC versions.

The first milestone is an "embedded Rust compiler" capable of compiling no_std programs that depend only on the core crate. The second is a "Rust for Linux compiler" that supports the alloc crate alongside the specific crates used by the kernel. The final milestone is a "general purpose compiler" aimed at handling broader Rust applications beyond the kernel environment.

The first milestone is not completely implemented, but it is close. Progress toward the Rust for Linux milestone is underway. In March, the team added support for compiler_builtins, a key low-level crate required by kernel builds, and focused on resolving problems within the kernel's ffi crate. To support this effort, Zhi Heng joined the project in May 2026 for an Open Source Security internship. His work is dedicated to fixing bugs encountered when gccrs compiles kernel crates and establishing continuous-integration testing to prevent regressions.

However, simply testing to ensure the compiler can process Rust code without crashing is only part of the task. The generated code must also be correct. The implementation of Rust's destructor semantics is key to the generation of correct code, because idiomatic Rust code uses them more heavily than traditional C code, so that has been another area of focus.

The Drop infrastructure

Rust manages resources using a scope-based model known as resource acquisition is initialization (RAII). When a value goes out of scope, the compiler automatically inserts a call to its destructor, which is defined by the Drop trait.

In Rust, tracking when variables must be cleaned up is complex because a variable's initialization state can change depending on the control flow within a function. If a variable is conditionally moved or only partially initialized, the compiler cannot simply drop it at the end of the enclosing scope. To solve this, the frontend must analyze the control-flow graph and generate dynamic "drop flags"—boolean variables tracked at run time—to record whether a value needs to be destroyed before passing this representation to the GCC backend. That analysis was missing from the initial implementation of Drop in gccrs, causing some Drop::drop() calls to be omitted or incorrect.

In the context of the Linux kernel, missing Drop calls lead to severe run-time failures, such as memory leaks or unreleased system resources. A primary example is lock management. When kernel code acquires a lock, the Rust for Linux API returns a MutexGuard. The Drop implementation for this guard is responsible for releasing the lock.

As the team noted in May, without proper Drop calls, the lock is never released. This results in miscompiled code where locks remain held after their guard goes out of scope, which can cause synchronization failures or deadlocks. Google Summer of Code (GSoC) participant Janet Chien joined the project in May to focus specifically on building the gccrs Drop infrastructure.

Name-resolution work

Testing the compiler against the standard library and kernel crates also exposed highlighted fundamental bugs in how gccrs handled name resolution, although the project was already aware of many of them, and had begun working on name-resolution in particular in 2023.

Rust maintains three distinct namespaces: the value namespace for functions and static variables, the macro namespace, and the type namespace for structures, modules, and traits. When the compiler encounters a "path"—a sequence of identifiers like crate::foo::bar used to refer to an item—it must identify the correct namespace for each segment of the path.

The development team discovered a flaw in its processing pipeline. Previously, when gccrs looked for the definition of an item, it resolved paths within the namespace of the target item type. For instance, when looking for a function, it resolved the path segments in the value namespace. This approach is incorrect because modules and publicly visible imports actually live in the type namespace; the compiler cannot successfully traverse a path to find a function without first resolving the module structure itself in the type namespace.

Fixing this problem required a rewrite of internal data structures and a refactoring of the visitor implementations used throughout the code. By May, these changes allowed the deeply nested imports in the core crate to resolve correctly. Modules and imports are now properly inserted into the types namespace, aligning gccrs more closely with rustc behavior.

Metadata and attribute handling

The shift to compiling kernel crates highlighted further problems in how gccrs processes compiler attributes and crate metadata.

Rust relies on attributes, such as #[cfg()], for conditional compilation. The February 2026 report, described how lead developer Pierre-Emmanuel Patry had reworked the attribute-handling pipeline. His work split, into two distinct passes, the compiler pass that removes items excluded by the cfg attribute. This separation was necessary to support unstable features within the kernel; some of these features rely on macro expansion or conditional attributes that must be stripped before the main attribute-validation pass can safely evaluate them without triggering compiler errors.

In March, gccrs added a command-line option equivalent to rustc's -Zcrate-attr, called -frust-crate-attr. This option allows the build system to inject attributes during compiler invocation without modifying the underlying source files. This is particularly useful for passing the #![no_core] attribute, which is necessary to compile code without depending on the standard core library. That feature is relied upon by developers who are fuzzing the compiler to locate edge-case bugs.

Linking the kernel's Rust crates eventually revealed a new bug. Rust crates export metadata, typically bundled in .rlib files, to communicate their public APIs to other crates. When attempting to link kernel code, the developers found that certain modules and exports were simply missing from the emitted metadata. Because the compiler was omitting nested module exports during metadata generation, gccrs was unable to resolve external dependencies.

This problem was not caught by the project's existing metadata test cases, which relied on flatter module structures. Identifying this bug required compiling real-world code. Consequently, the team began a significant rework of the metadata handling system to ensure the GNU toolchain can successfully link the kernel's dependency tree.

Current capabilities and the challenges of upstreaming

So, what is possible for gccrs today? Currently, the compiler can successfully handle standalone no_core programs, and has made significant strides in processing the core crate and implementing compiler builtins. However, fully compiling the kernel's complex Rust abstractions remains a work in progress. gccrs is currently able to parse the kernel's code and the project is focused on correctly implementing the run-time semantics.

Beyond technical hurdles, gccrs has also had to navigate the organization challenges of the GNU toolchain. Historically, the project has faced problems landing its patches in the upstream GCC tree. Integrating an entirely new, rapidly evolving language frontend into GCC is a large undertaking, and the size of the patch sets has occasionally overwhelmed the limited bandwidth of upstream GCC reviewers. While the situation has improved as the frontend's architecture has stabilized, merging sweeping changes—such as the recent name-resolution rewrites and Drop infrastructure—still requires significant coordination and patience to clear the upstream review process the bigger change is the recent elevation of two gccrs developers to the status of GCC maintainers, which allows them to stage updates in their own tree and then push them wholesale.

Next steps

Work continues on the remaining components required to compile the kernel. GSoC participant Enes Çevik, who also joined the project in May, is implementing support for the alloc crate. This crate handles dynamic memory allocation types like Box, Rc, and Vec. Although kernel development avoids many standard library abstractions, several core kernel Rust abstractions rely on allocation types, making support for the alloc crate a hard prerequisite for the "Rust for Linux" milestone.

The broader development community will soon receive a closer look at this progress. Patry and Arthur Cohen plan to present a talk titled "Compiling the Linux kernel with gccrs" at RustConf in Montreal and EuroRust in Barcelona later this year. By systematically addressing the specific requirements of kernel code, the project is steadily building the foundation for using GCC to compile Rust code within the Linux kernel ecosystem.

To solve this, the frontend must analyze the control-flow graph and generate dynamic "drop flags"—boolean variables tracked at run time—to record whether a value needs to be destroyed before passing this representation to the GCC backend. That analysis was missing from the initial implementation of Drop in gccrs, causing some Drop::drop() calls to be omitted or incorrect.

sentences.en: In Rust, tracking when variables must be cleaned up is complex because a variable's initialization state can change depending on the control flow within a function.
sentences.zh: 在 Rust 中，跟踪何时必须清理变量很复杂，因为变量的初始化状态可能会根据函数内的控制流而改变。

sentences.en: If a variable is conditionally moved or only partially initialized, the compiler cannot simply drop it at the end of the enclosing scope.
sentences.zh: 如果有条件地移动变量或仅部分初始化变量，则编译器不能简单地将其删除到封闭范围的末尾。

sentences.en: To solve this, the frontend must analyze the control-flow graph and generate dynamic "drop flags"—boolean variables tracked at run time—to record whether a value needs to be destroyed before passing this representation to the GCC backend.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，前端必须分析控制流图并生成动态“删除标志”（在运行时跟踪的布尔变量），以记录在将此表示形式传递到 GCC 后端之前是否需要销毁某个值。

sentences.en: That analysis was missing from the initial implementation of Drop in gccrs, causing some Drop::drop() calls to be omitted or incorrect.
sentences.zh: gccrs 中 Drop 的初始实现中缺少该分析，导致某些 Drop::drop() 调用被省略或不正确。

blocks.html_en: In the context of the Linux kernel, missing Drop calls lead to severe run-time failures, such as memory leaks or unreleased system resources. A primary example is lock management. When kernel code acquires a lock, the Rust for Linux API returns a MutexGuard. The Drop implementation for this guard is responsible for releasing the lock.

sentences.en: In the context of the Linux kernel, missing Drop calls lead to severe run-time failures, such as memory leaks or unreleased system resources.
sentences.zh: 在 Linux 内核的上下文中，丢失 Drop 调用会导致严重的运行时故障，例如内存泄漏或未释放的系统资源。

sentences.en: A primary example is lock management.
sentences.zh: 一个主要的例子是锁管理。

sentences.en: When kernel code acquires a lock, the Rust for Linux API returns a MutexGuard.
sentences.zh: 当内核代码获取锁时，Rust for Linux API 返回一个 MutexGuard。

sentences.en: The Drop implementation for this guard is responsible for releasing the lock.
sentences.zh: 该守卫的 Drop 实现负责释放锁。

blocks.html_en: As the team noted in May, without proper Drop calls, the lock is never released. This results in miscompiled code where locks remain held after their guard goes out of scope, which can cause synchronization failures or deadlocks. Google Summer of Code (GSoC) participant Janet Chien joined the project in May to focus specifically on building the gccrs Drop infrastructure.

sentences.en: As the team noted in May, without proper Drop calls, the lock is never released.
sentences.zh: 正如该团队在 5 月份指出的那样，如果没有适当的 Drop 调用，锁就永远不会被释放。

sentences.en: This results in miscompiled code where locks remain held after their guard goes out of scope, which can cause synchronization failures or deadlocks.
sentences.zh: 这会导致错误编译的代码，在其防护超出范围后，锁仍然保留，这可能会导致同步失败或死锁。

sentences.en: Google Summer of Code (GSoC) participant Janet Chien joined the project in May to focus specifically on building the gccrs Drop infrastructure.
sentences.zh: Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 参与者 Janet Chien 于 5 月加入该项目，专门致力于构建 gccrs Drop 基础设施。

blocks.html_en: Name-resolution work

sentences.en: Name-resolution work
sentences.zh: 名称解析工作

blocks.html_en: Testing the compiler against the standard library and kernel crates also exposed highlighted fundamental bugs in how gccrs handled name resolution, although the project was already aware of many of them, and had begun working on name-resolution in particular in 2023.

sentences.en: Testing the compiler against the standard library and kernel crates also exposed highlighted fundamental bugs in how gccrs handled name resolution, although the project was already aware of many of them, and had begun working on name-resolution in particular in 2023.
sentences.zh: 针对标准库和内核包测试编译器还暴露了 gccrs 如何处理名称解析的突出基本错误，尽管该项目已经意识到其中的许多错误，并且特别是在 2023 年开始致力于名称解析。

blocks.html_en: Rust maintains three distinct namespaces: the value namespace for functions and static variables, the macro namespace, and the type namespace for structures, modules, and traits. When the compiler encounters a "path"—a sequence of identifiers like crate::foo::bar used to refer to an item—it must identify the correct namespace for each segment of the path.

sentences.en: Rust maintains three distinct namespaces: the value namespace for functions and static variables, the macro namespace, and the type namespace for structures, modules, and traits.
sentences.zh: Rust 维护三个不同的命名空间：函数和静态变量的值命名空间、宏命名空间以及结构、模块和特征的类型命名空间。

sentences.en: When the compiler encounters a "path"—a sequence of identifiers like crate::foo::bar used to refer to an item—it must identify the correct namespace for each segment of the path.
sentences.zh: 当编译器遇到“路径”（一系列标识符，如 crate::foo::bar 用于引用某个项目）时，它必须为路径的每个段标识正确的命名空间。

blocks.html_en: The development team discovered a flaw in its processing pipeline. Previously, when gccrs looked for the definition of an item, it resolved paths within the namespace of the target item type. For instance, when looking for a function, it resolved the path segments in the value namespace. This approach is incorrect because modules and publicly visible imports actually live in the type namespace; the compiler cannot successfully traverse a path to find a function without first resolving the module structure itself in the type namespace.

sentences.en: The development team discovered a flaw in its processing pipeline.
sentences.zh: 开发团队在其处理流程中发现了一个缺陷。

sentences.en: Previously, when gccrs looked for the definition of an item, it resolved paths within the namespace of the target item type.
sentences.zh: 以前，当 gccrs 查找项目的定义时，它会解析目标项目类型的命名空间内的路径。

sentences.en: For instance, when looking for a function, it resolved the path segments in the value namespace.
sentences.zh: 例如，当查找函数时，它解析值命名空间中的路径段。

sentences.en: This approach is incorrect because modules and publicly visible imports actually live in the type namespace; the compiler cannot successfully traverse a path to find a function without first resolving the module structure itself in the type namespace.
sentences.zh: 这种方法是不正确的，因为模块和公开可见的导入实际上位于类型命名空间中；如果不首先在类型命名空间中解析模块结构本身，编译器就无法成功遍历路径来查找函数。

blocks.html_en: Fixing this problem required a rewrite of internal data structures and a refactoring of the visitor implementations used throughout the code. By May, these changes allowed the deeply nested imports in the core crate to resolve correctly. Modules and imports are now properly inserted into the types namespace, aligning gccrs more closely with rustc behavior.

sentences.en: Fixing this problem required a rewrite of internal data structures and a refactoring of the visitor implementations used throughout the code.
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题需要重写内部数据结构并重构整个代码中使用的访问者实现。

sentences.en: By May, these changes allowed the deeply nested imports in the core crate to resolve correctly.
sentences.zh: 到 5 月份，这些更改使得核心包中的深层嵌套导入能够正确解析。

sentences.en: Modules and imports are now properly inserted into the types namespace, aligning gccrs more closely with rustc behavior.
sentences.zh: 模块和导入现在已正确插入到 types 命名空间中，使 gccrs 与 rustc 行为更加紧密地保持一致。

blocks.html_en: Metadata and attribute handling

sentences.en: Metadata and attribute handling
sentences.zh: 元数据和属性处理

blocks.html_en: The shift to compiling kernel crates highlighted further problems in how gccrs processes compiler attributes and crate metadata.

sentences.en: The shift to compiling kernel crates highlighted further problems in how gccrs processes compiler attributes and crate metadata.
sentences.zh: 转向编译内核 crate 进一步凸显了 gccrs 如何处理编译器属性和 crate 元数据的问题。

blocks.html_en: Rust relies on attributes, such as #[cfg()], for conditional compilation. The February 2026 report, described how lead developer Pierre-Emmanuel Patry had reworked the attribute-handling pipeline. His work split, into two distinct passes, the compiler pass that removes items excluded by the cfg attribute. This separation was necessary to support unstable features within the kernel; some of these features rely on macro expansion or conditional attributes that must be stripped before the main attribute-validation pass can safely evaluate them without triggering compiler errors.

sentences.en: Rust relies on attributes, such as #[cfg()], for conditional compilation.
sentences.zh: Rust 依赖属性（例如 #[cfg()]）进行条件编译。

sentences.en: The February 2026 report, described how lead developer Pierre-Emmanuel Patry had reworked the attribute-handling pipeline.
sentences.zh: 2026 年 2 月的报告描述了首席开发人员 Pierre-Emmanuel Patry 如何重新设计属性处理管道。

sentences.en: His work split, into two distinct passes, the compiler pass that removes items excluded by the cfg attribute.
sentences.zh: 他的工作分为两个不同的阶段，编译器阶段删除 cfg 属性排除的项目。

sentences.en: This separation was necessary to support unstable features within the kernel; some of these features rely on macro expansion or conditional attributes that must be stripped before the main attribute-validation pass can safely evaluate them without triggering compiler errors.
sentences.zh: 这种分离对于支持内核中不稳定的功能是必要的；其中一些功能依赖于宏扩展或条件属性，在主属性验证过程可以安全地评估它们而不触发编译器错误之前必须将其剥离。

blocks.html_en: In March, gccrs added a command-line option equivalent to rustc's -Zcrate-attr, called -frust-crate-attr. This option allows the build system to inject attributes during compiler invocation without modifying the underlying source files. This is particularly useful for passing the #![no_core] attribute, which is necessary to compile code without depending on the standard core library. That feature is relied upon by developers who are fuzzing the compiler to locate edge-case bugs.

sentences.en: In March, gccrs added a command-line option equivalent to rustc's -Zcrate-attr, called -frust-crate-attr.
sentences.zh: 3 月份，gccrs 添加了一个相当于 rustc 的 -Zcrate-attr 的命令行选项，称为 -frust-crate-attr。

sentences.en: This option allows the build system to inject attributes during compiler invocation without modifying the underlying source files.
sentences.zh: 此选项允许构建系统在编译器调用期间注入属性，而无需修改底层源文件。

sentences.en: This is particularly useful for passing the #![no_core] attribute, which is necessary to compile code without depending on the standard core library.
sentences.zh: 这对于传递 #![no_core] 属性特别有用，这是在不依赖标准核心库的情况下编译代码所必需的。

sentences.en: That feature is relied upon by developers who are fuzzing the compiler to locate edge-case bugs.
sentences.zh: 开发人员依赖该功能对编译器进行模糊测试以定位边缘情况错误。

blocks.html_en: Linking the kernel's Rust crates eventually revealed a new bug. Rust crates export metadata, typically bundled in .rlib files, to communicate their public APIs to other crates. When attempting to link kernel code, the developers found that certain modules and exports were simply missing from the emitted metadata. Because the compiler was omitting nested module exports during metadata generation, gccrs was unable to resolve external dependencies.

sentences.en: Linking the kernel's Rust crates eventually revealed a new bug.
sentences.zh: 链接内核的 Rust 包最终发现了一个新的错误。

sentences.en: Rust crates export metadata, typically bundled in .rlib files, to communicate their public APIs to other crates.
sentences.zh: Rust crate 导出元数据（通常捆绑在 .rlib 文件中），以将其公共 API 传达给其他 crate。

sentences.en: When attempting to link kernel code, the developers found that certain modules and exports were simply missing from the emitted metadata.
sentences.zh: 当尝试链接内核代码时，开发人员发现发出的元数据中根本缺少某些模块和导出。

sentences.en: Because the compiler was omitting nested module exports during metadata generation, gccrs was unable to resolve external dependencies.
sentences.zh: 由于编译器在元数据生成期间省略了嵌套模块导出，因此 gccrs 无法解析外部依赖项。

blocks.html_en: This problem was not caught by the project's existing metadata test cases, which relied on flatter module structures. Identifying this bug required compiling real-world code. Consequently, the team began a significant rework of the metadata handling system to ensure the GNU toolchain can successfully link the kernel's dependency tree.

sentences.en: This problem was not caught by the project's existing metadata test cases, which relied on flatter module structures.
sentences.zh: 该项目现有的元数据测试用例没有发现这个问题，该测试用例依赖于更扁平的模块结构。

sentences.en: Identifying this bug required compiling real-world code.
sentences.zh: 识别此错误需要编译实际代码。

sentences.en: Consequently, the team began a significant rework of the metadata handling system to ensure the GNU toolchain can successfully link the kernel's dependency tree.
sentences.zh: 因此，团队开始对元数据处理系统进行重大修改，以确保 GNU 工具链能够成功链接内核的依赖树。

blocks.html_en: Current capabilities and the challenges of upstreaming

sentences.en: Current capabilities and the challenges of upstreaming
sentences.zh: 当前的能力和上游的挑战

blocks.html_en: So, what is possible for gccrs today? Currently, the compiler can successfully handle standalone no_core programs, and has made significant strides in processing the core crate and implementing compiler builtins. However, fully compiling the kernel's complex Rust abstractions remains a work in progress. gccrs is currently able to parse the kernel's code and the project is focused on correctly implementing the run-time semantics.

sentences.en: So, what is possible for gccrs today?
sentences.zh: 那么，今天的 gccrs 有什么可能呢？

sentences.en: Currently, the compiler can successfully handle standalone no_core programs, and has made significant strides in processing the core crate and implementing compiler builtins.
sentences.zh: 目前，编译器可以成功处理独立的 no_core 程序，并且在处理核心包和实现编译器内置方面取得了重大进展。

sentences.en: However, fully compiling the kernel's complex Rust abstractions remains a work in progress.
sentences.zh: 然而，完全编译内核的复杂 Rust 抽象仍然是一项正在进行的工作。

sentences.en: gccrs is currently able to parse the kernel's code and the project is focused on correctly implementing the run-time semantics.
sentences.zh: gccrs 目前能够解析内核的代码，该项目的重点是正确实现运行时语义。

blocks.html_en: Beyond technical hurdles, gccrs has also had to navigate the organization challenges of the GNU toolchain. Historically, the project has faced problems landing its patches in the upstream GCC tree. Integrating an entirely new, rapidly evolving language frontend into GCC is a large undertaking, and the size of the patch sets has occasionally overwhelmed the limited bandwidth of upstream GCC reviewers. While the situation has improved as the frontend's architecture has stabilized, merging sweeping changes—such as the recent name-resolution rewrites and Drop infrastructure—still requires significant coordination and patience to clear the upstream review process the bigger change is the recent elevation of two gccrs developers to the status of GCC maintainers, which allows them to stage updates in their own tree and then push them wholesale.

sentences.en: Beyond technical hurdles, gccrs has also had to navigate the organization challenges of the GNU toolchain.
sentences.zh: 除了技术障碍之外，gccrs 还必须应对 GNU 工具链的组织挑战。

sentences.en: Historically, the project has faced problems landing its patches in the upstream GCC tree.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，该项目在将其补丁放到上游 GCC 树中时遇到过问题。

sentences.en: Integrating an entirely new, rapidly evolving language frontend into GCC is a large undertaking, and the size of the patch sets has occasionally overwhelmed the limited bandwidth of upstream GCC reviewers.
sentences.zh: 将一个全新的、快速发展的语言前端集成到 GCC 中是一项艰巨的任务，补丁集的大小有时会超出上游 GCC 审阅者的有限带宽。

sentences.en: While the situation has improved as the frontend's architecture has stabilized, merging sweeping changes—such as the recent name-resolution rewrites and Drop infrastructure—still requires significant coordination and patience to clear the upstream review process the bigger change is the recent elevation of two gccrs developers to the status of GCC maintainers, which allows them to stage updates in their own tree and then push them wholesale.
sentences.zh: 虽然随着前端架构的稳定，情况有所改善，但合并彻底的变化（例如最近的名称解析重写和 Drop 基础设施）仍然需要大量的协调和耐心来清理上游审查流程，更大的变化是最近将两名 gccrs 开发人员提升为 GCC 维护者的地位，这允许他们在自己的树中暂存更新，然后批量推送。

blocks.html_en: Next steps

sentences.en: Next steps
sentences.zh: 后续步骤

blocks.html_en: Work continues on the remaining components required to compile the kernel. GSoC participant Enes Çevik, who also joined the project in May, is implementing support for the alloc crate. This crate handles dynamic memory allocation types like Box, Rc, and Vec. Although kernel development avoids many standard library abstractions, several core kernel Rust abstractions rely on allocation types, making support for the alloc crate a hard prerequisite for the "Rust for Linux" milestone.

sentences.en: Work continues on the remaining components required to compile the kernel.
sentences.zh: 编译内核所需的其余组件的工作仍在继续。

sentences.en: GSoC participant Enes Çevik, who also joined the project in May, is implementing support for the alloc crate.
sentences.zh: GSoC 参与者 Enes Çevik 也在 5 月份加入了该项目，他正在实施对 alloc crate 的支持。

sentences.en: This crate handles dynamic memory allocation types like Box, Rc, and Vec.
sentences.zh: 该包处理动态内存分配类型，如 Box、Rc 和 Vec。

sentences.en: Although kernel development avoids many standard library abstractions, several core kernel Rust abstractions rely on allocation types, making support for the alloc crate a hard prerequisite for the "Rust for Linux" milestone.
sentences.zh: 尽管内核开发避免了许多标准库抽象，但几个核心内核 Rust 抽象依赖于分配类型，这使得对 alloc crate 的支持成为“Rust for Linux”里程碑的硬性先决条件。

blocks.html_en: The broader development community will soon receive a closer look at this progress. Patry and Arthur Cohen plan to present a talk titled "Compiling the Linux kernel with gccrs" at RustConf in Montreal and EuroRust in Barcelona later this year. By systematically addressing the specific requirements of kernel code, the project is steadily building the foundation for using GCC to compile Rust code within the Linux kernel ecosystem.

sentences.en: The broader development community will soon receive a closer look at this progress.
sentences.zh: 更广泛的开发社区很快就会更仔细地了解这一进展。

sentences.en: Patry and Arthur Cohen plan to present a talk titled "Compiling the Linux kernel with gccrs" at RustConf in Montreal and EuroRust in Barcelona later this year.
sentences.zh: Patry 和 Arthur Cohen 计划于今年晚些时候在蒙特利尔的 RustConf 和巴塞罗那的 EuroRust 上发表题为“使用 gccrs 编译 Linux 内核”的演讲。

sentences.en: By systematically addressing the specific requirements of kernel code, the project is steadily building the foundation for using GCC to compile Rust code within the Linux kernel ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 通过系统地解决内核代码的具体要求，该项目正在稳步构建在 Linux 内核生态系统中使用 GCC 编译 Rust 代码的基础。

content_html_zh:
[LWN 订阅者专用内容]

欢迎来到 LWN.net 以下仅供订阅的内容由 LWN 订阅者提供给您。 成千上万的订阅者依靠 LWN 获取来自 Linux 和自由软件社区的最佳新闻。 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑订阅 LWN。 感谢您访问LWN.net！

gccrs 项目正在为 GCC 编译器创建 Rust 前端，该项目在 2026 年上半年专注于编译 Linux 内核。 通过针对内核包测试编译器，开发团队在为其他 Rust 程序生成正确代码方面取得了重大进展。 正如该项目的每周和每月报告中详细介绍的那样，这项工作发现并解决了属性处理（二月份的报告中描述）、名称解析和资源管理（五月份的报告中详细介绍）等领域的问题。 目前，编译器只能处理简单的独立程序，但这种情况可能在未来几个月内迅速改变。

编译 Linux 内核 Rust 组件的动力源于 Rust 引入内核带来的新工具链要求。 目前，开发人员必须使用基于 LLVM 的 rustc 编译器（尽管 rustc 确实有实验性的、正在进行中的支持，通过 rust_codegen_gcc 使用 GCC 作为后端）。 虽然内核支持 LLVM，但需要基于 GCC 的替代方案来支持 LLVM 未针对的架构并与 GCC 现有的插件生态系统集成。 随着内核 Rust 集成的成熟，工具链的灵活性和基于 GCC 的编译器的可用性已成为 Linux 发行版的优先事项。

重组里程碑

编译器前端项目通常会根据目标后端的发布周期来跟踪其进度。 在 2026 年 3 月的报告中，gccrs 团队宣布了项目管理的改变，选择将其工作组织为三个基于能力的里程碑，而不是针对特定的 GCC 版本。

第一个里程碑是“嵌入式 Rust 编译器”，能够编译仅依赖于核心包的 no_std 程序。 第二个是“Rust for Linux 编译器”，它支持 alloc crate 以及内核使用的特定 crate。 最后一个里程碑是“通用编译器”，旨在处理内核环境之外更广泛的 Rust 应用程序。

第一个里程碑尚未完全实现，但已经接近了。 Rust for Linux 里程碑的进展正在进行中。 3 月份，该团队添加了对 compiler_builtins（内核构建所需的关键低级 crate）的支持，并专注于解决内核 ffi crate 中的问题。 为了支持这项工作，智恒于 2026 年 5 月加入该项目，进行开源安全实习。 他的工作致力于修复 gccrs 编译内核包时遇到的错误并建立持续集成测试以防止回归。

然而，简单地测试以确保编译器可以处理 Rust 代码而不崩溃只是任务的一部分。 生成的代码也必须正确。 Rust 析构函数语义的实现是生成正确代码的关键，因为惯用的 Rust 代码比传统 C 代码更频繁地使用它们，因此这是另一个重点领域。

Drop 基础设施

Rust 使用基于范围的模型来管理资源，称为资源获取即初始化 (RAII)。 当值超出范围时，编译器会自动插入对其析构函数的调用，该调用由 Drop 特征定义。

在 Rust 中，跟踪何时必须清理变量很复杂，因为变量的初始化状态可能会根据函数内的控制流而改变。 如果有条件地移动变量或仅部分初始化变量，则编译器不能简单地将其删除到封闭范围的末尾。 为了解决这个问题，前端必须分析控制流图并生成动态“删除标志”（在运行时跟踪的布尔变量），以记录在将此表示形式传递到 GCC 后端之前是否需要销毁某个值。 gccrs 中 Drop 的初始实现中缺少该分析，导致某些 Drop::drop() 调用被省略或不正确。

在 Linux 内核的上下文中，丢失 Drop 调用会导致严重的运行时故障，例如内存泄漏或未释放的系统资源。 一个主要的例子是锁管理。 当内核代码获取锁时，Rust for Linux API 返回一个 MutexGuard。 该守卫的 Drop 实现负责释放锁。

正如该团队在 5 月份指出的那样，如果没有适当的 Drop 调用，锁就永远不会被释放。 这会导致错误编译的代码，在其防护超出范围后，锁仍然保留，这可能会导致同步失败或死锁。 Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 参与者 Janet Chien 于 5 月加入该项目，专门致力于构建 gccrs Drop 基础设施。

名称解析工作

针对标准库和内核包测试编译器还暴露了 gccrs 如何处理名称解析的突出基本错误，尽管该项目已经意识到其中的许多错误，并且特别是在 2023 年开始致力于名称解析。

Rust 维护三个不同的命名空间：函数和静态变量的值命名空间、宏命名空间以及结构、模块和特征的类型命名空间。 当编译器遇到“路径”（一系列标识符，如 crate::foo::bar 用于引用某个项目）时，它必须为路径的每个段标识正确的命名空间。

开发团队在其处理流程中发现了一个缺陷。 以前，当 gccrs 查找项目的定义时，它会解析目标项目类型的命名空间内的路径。 例如，当查找函数时，它解析值命名空间中的路径段。 这种方法是不正确的，因为模块和公开可见的导入实际上位于类型命名空间中；如果不首先在类型命名空间中解析模块结构本身，编译器就无法成功遍历路径来查找函数。

解决这个问题需要重写内部数据结构并重构整个代码中使用的访问者实现。 到 5 月份，这些更改使得核心包中的深层嵌套导入能够正确解析。 模块和导入现在已正确插入到 types 命名空间中，使 gccrs 与 rustc 行为更加紧密地保持一致。

元数据和属性处理

转向编译内核 crate 进一步凸显了 gccrs 如何处理编译器属性和 crate 元数据的问题。

Rust 依赖属性（例如 #[cfg()]）进行条件编译。 2026 年 2 月的报告描述了首席开发人员 Pierre-Emmanuel Patry 如何重新设计属性处理管道。 他的工作分为两个不同的阶段，编译器阶段删除 cfg 属性排除的项目。 这种分离对于支持内核中不稳定的功能是必要的；其中一些功能依赖于宏扩展或条件属性，在主属性验证过程可以安全地评估它们而不触发编译器错误之前必须将其剥离。

3 月份，gccrs 添加了一个相当于 rustc 的 -Zcrate-attr 的命令行选项，称为 -frust-crate-attr。 此选项允许构建系统在编译器调用期间注入属性，而无需修改底层源文件。 这对于传递 #![no_core] 属性特别有用，这是在不依赖标准核心库的情况下编译代码所必需的。 开发人员依赖该功能对编译器进行模糊测试以定位边缘情况错误。

链接内核的 Rust 包最终发现了一个新的错误。 Rust crate 导出元数据（通常捆绑在 .rlib 文件中），以将其公共 API 传达给其他 crate。 当尝试链接内核代码时，开发人员发现发出的元数据中根本缺少某些模块和导出。 由于编译器在元数据生成期间省略了嵌套模块导出，因此 gccrs 无法解析外部依赖项。

该项目现有的元数据测试用例没有发现这个问题，该测试用例依赖于更扁平的模块结构。 识别此错误需要编译实际代码。 因此，团队开始对元数据处理系统进行重大修改，以确保 GNU 工具链能够成功链接内核的依赖树。

当前的能力和上游的挑战

那么，今天的 gccrs 有什么可能呢？ 目前，编译器可以成功处理独立的 no_core 程序，并且在处理核心包和实现编译器内置方面取得了重大进展。 然而，完全编译内核的复杂 Rust 抽象仍然是一项正在进行的工作。 gccrs 目前能够解析内核的代码，该项目的重点是正确实现运行时语义。

除了技术障碍之外，gccrs 还必须应对 GNU 工具链的组织挑战。 从历史上看，该项目在将其补丁放到上游 GCC 树中时遇到过问题。 将一个全新的、快速发展的语言前端集成到 GCC 中是一项艰巨的任务，补丁集的大小有时会超出上游 GCC 审阅者的有限带宽。 虽然随着前端架构的稳定，情况有所改善，但合并彻底的变化（例如最近的名称解析重写和 Drop 基础设施）仍然需要大量的协调和耐心来清理上游审查流程，更大的变化是最近将两名 gccrs 开发人员提升为 GCC 维护者的地位，这允许他们在自己的树中暂存更新，然后批量推送。

后续步骤

编译内核所需的其余组件的工作仍在继续。 GSoC 参与者 Enes Çevik 也在 5 月份加入了该项目，他正在实施对 alloc crate 的支持。 该包处理动态内存分配类型，如 Box、Rc 和 Vec。 尽管内核开发避免了许多标准库抽象，但几个核心内核 Rust 抽象依赖于分配类型，这使得对 alloc crate 的支持成为“Rust for Linux”里程碑的硬性先决条件。

更广泛的开发社区很快就会更仔细地了解这一进展。 Patry 和 Arthur Cohen 计划于今年晚些时候在蒙特利尔的 RustConf 和巴塞罗那的 EuroRust 上发表题为“使用 gccrs 编译 Linux 内核”的演讲。 通过系统地解决内核代码的具体要求，该项目正在稳步构建在 Linux 内核生态系统中使用 GCC 编译 Rust 代码的基础。
